questions.question_english: What is the fundamental principle laid down in the DSEA 1973 regarding the commercialization of education?
options_english: Schools can operate for profit provided it is disclosed in official prospectus.
Education is charitable; schools cannot operate for profit to individuals or groups.
Schools can distribute up to ten percent profit to managing committee members.
Independent unaided private schools are completely exempt from non-profit rules.
questions.explanation_english: The principle reflected in the Act is that recognised school education is to be run for educational and charitable purposes, not as a mechanism to distribute profits to individuals or groups. Fees and other receipts should be applied to legitimate school expenses, facilities, staff and educational objectives, subject to financial rules and oversight. Publication of a profit-making intention or an unaided status does not automatically exempt a school from applicable non-commercial and accounting obligations.

questions.explanation_english: A is false but R is true Under Article 30(1) of the Constitution and Section 2(o) of the Delhi School Education Act, 1973, minority status is conferred on educational institutions established by either religious or linguistic minorities.
